message.content:
Build a small coordination CLI called `hq` for a hackathon repo where 2 humans each run several coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) coordinated through GitHub Issues. Work in /Users/ellishewes/conductor/workspaces/durhack-proj/cayenne. Be fast; a teammate is waiting.

CREATE ONLY THESE FILES (other people are editing other files in this same directory right now; do not touch anything else, do not run `git add/commit/push/switch`, and do not run any `gh` command that writes to GitHub — read-only gh like `gh pr list --json` with no fields, to see available fields, is fine; the GitHub repo ehewes/durhack-proj currently has no issues/PRs and its remote is empty):
- `hq` (POSIX sh shim, chmod +x): `#!/bin/sh` then `exec python3 "$(dirname "$0")/tools/hq/hq.py" "$@"`
- `hq.cmd` (Windows shim): `@python "%~dp0tools\hq\hq.py" %*`
- `hq.json`: `{"default_branch": "main", "lanes": {}, "check": [], "setup": [], "stale_minutes": 60}` (lanes format: `{"<lane>": {"owner": "<github login>", "paths": ["dir/"]}}`)
- `tools/hq/hq.py` (python3 stdlib only, MUST run on Python 3.9: no `match`, no PEP 604 unions at runtime, `from __future__ import annotations` is fine; argparse subcommands)
- `tools/hq/tests/test_hq.py` (unittest; import hq.py via importlib from its path). TDD: write tests for the pure logic first, then implement. Run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/hq/tests -v` until green.

Design: pure functions (parsing/decisions, unit-tested, take plain dicts/lists) separated from I/O (`gh`/`git` via subprocess, JSON output). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 refused by a gate, 3 lost a claim race. Output plain and short (agents read it); symbols ✓ ✗ ! allowed. Repo root = `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; config read from `<root>/hq.json`. owner/repo from `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner`.

Issue body format (GitHub issue forms render each field as `### <label>` then the value; empty optional fields render as `_No response_`, treat that as empty). Headings: `### Goal`, `### Acceptance criteria`, `### Scope`, `### Do not touch`, `### Blocked by`, `### Verify`, `### Notes`. `Blocked by` contains refs like `#12, #14` or `none`. `Scope` contains paths/globs (e.g. `web/src/`, `api/*.py`), one per line or comma separated, possibly in backticks or as `- ` bullets.

Identity: login = `gh api user --jq .login` (cache per process); agent = `--agent` or env HQ_AGENT (default `agent`); workspace = `--workspace` or env CONDUCTOR_WORKSPACE_NAME or basename of the worktree root. id = `<login>/<agent>/<workspace>`.

Claim protocol (race-safe without a lock; two humans): claim comment body starts with `<!-- hq:claim id=<id> branch=<branch> -->` then a line like `Claimed by **<login>** via `<agent>` (workspace `<ws>`) on branch `<branch>``. Release comment starts with `<!-- hq:release id=<id> -->` + optional note. Active claims = claim markers with no LATER release marker for the same id (comment order / createdAt). Winner = earliest active claim (createdAt, tie -> list order).

Commands:
1. `setup [--check | --ci]`. Checklist with ✓/✗/! (warning) and a fix hint per item: python>=3.9; `gh` installed and `gh auth status` ok; `gh repo view` works; `git config user.email` set; `entire --version` works (! if missing, hint: brew install --cask entireio/tap/entire); `<root>/.entire/settings.json` has `checkpoints.primary.type == "git-branch"` (! otherwise, hint `entire configure --checkpoint-backend branch`); guard installed: `<git-common-dir>/hooks/pre-commit` contains marker `hq-guard`; `git config --get gc.auto` == `0`; if env CONDUCTOR_ROOT_PATH is set, `$CONDUCTOR_ROOT_PATH/.codex/hooks.json` exists (! hint: `git -C "$CONDUCTOR_ROOT_PATH" pull --ff-only` so Codex finds its hooks); ! if current branch is the default branch. Default mode (no flag) FIXES what it can, then prints the checklist: install guard shim into the shared hooks dir (`git rev-parse --git-common-dir` + `/hooks/pre-commit`): if absent write
   ```
   #!/bin/sh
   # hq-guard: run the versioned guard
   root="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
   if [ -x "$root/.githooks/pre-commit" ]; then "$root/.githooks/pre-commit" "$@" || exit $?; fi
   [ -x "$(dirname "$0")/pre-commit.local" ] && exec "$(dirname "$0")/pre-commit.local" "$@"
   exit 0
   ```
   and chmod +x; if a pre-commit exists WITHOUT the marker, move it to `pre-commit.local` first (keeps chaining). Set `git config gc.auto 0`. Run each `hq.json` `setup` command (shell=True) and report. `--check` only reports (exit 1 if any ✗; warnings don't fail). `--ci` only runs `hq.json` setup commands (no gh/git checks).
2. `bootstrap` (idempotent, run once per repo): labels via `gh label create NAME --color HEX --description D --force`: status:ready(0e8a16) status:in-progress(fbca04) status:review(1d76db) status:blocked(b60205) status:needs-human(5319e7) P0(b60205,"Demo-critical") P1(d93f0b) P2(c2e0c6) size:S(c5def5,"<=30 min of agent time") size:M(bfd4f2,"<=90 min") size:L(5319e7,"Too big: split it") type:feat type:bug type:chore type:spike type:docs review:pass(0e8a16) review:changes(d93f0b) agent:claude agent:codex agent:cursor epic, plus `lane:<name>` for each hq.json lane. Milestones (create missing via `gh api repos/{o}/{r}/milestones`): "M0 Skeleton", "M1 MVP demo path", "M2 Prizes + polish", "M3 Submission". Repo settings: `gh api -X PATCH repos/{o}/{r} -F allow_squash_merge=true -F allow_merge_commit=false -F allow_rebase_merge=false -F delete_branch_on_merge=true -f squash_merge_commit_title=PR_TITLE -f squash_merge_commit_message=COMMIT_MESSAGES` (keeps Entire-Checkpoint trailers in squash commits). Ruleset: if none named `hq-protect-main` exists (`gh api repos/{o}/{r}/rulesets`), POST JSON via `gh api -X POST repos/{o}/{r}/rulesets --input -`: name hq-protect-main, target branch, enforcement active, conditions.ref_name.include ["~DEFAULT_BRANCH"] exclude [], rules: deletion, non_fast_forward, pull_request with parameters {required_approving_review_count:0, dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push:false, require_code_owner_review:false, require_last_push_approval:false, required_review_thread_resolution:false}. If GitHub refuses (403/422, e.g. private repo without Pro), print `! ruleset unavailable: <reason>; the pre-commit guard is the protection` and continue. Print a summary.
3. `board [--brief]`: data from `gh issue list --state open --limit 200 --json number,title,labels,assignees,updatedAt,body` and `gh pr list --state open --limit 100 --json number,title,headRefName,isDraft,labels,statusCheckRollup,mergeable,updatedAt,files,closingIssuesReferences` (verify `files` is a valid list field; if not, fetch files per PR with `gh pr view N --json files`). For in-progress issues, get the active claim id from comments (`gh issue view N --json comments`; skip this in --brief). Sections: IN PROGRESS (#, title, claimer id or assignee, age, linked PR), REVIEW (PR #, issue, CI ✓/✗/…, review:pass/changes, draft, CONFLICTING), NEEDS HUMAN, BLOCKED (with open blockers), READY (sorted lane, then P0<P1<P2<none, then S<M<L), OVERLAPS (files touched by more than one open PR, with PR numbers), STALE (in-progress with updatedAt older than stale_minutes). `--brief`: at most ~15 lines (counts, in-progress list, overlaps, top 5 ready).
4. `claim N --agent A [--workspace W]`: fetch `gh issue view N --json number,title,body,state,labels,assignees,comments,url`. Refuse (exit 2) if not OPEN; if any `Blocked by` ref is still OPEN (check each with `gh issue view R --json state`); if another id holds an active claim (say who and since when). If my id already holds it, say so and continue (idempotent). If current branch is the default branch or detached, `git switch -c <login>/<N>-<slug>` (slug: lowercase alnum and hyphens from title, max 40 chars). Post claim comment (`gh issue comment N --body-file -`), re-fetch comments; if the winner is not me, post my release marker with note `lost race to <winner>` and exit 3. Then `gh issue edit N --add-assignee @me --add-label status:in-progress --remove-label status:ready` and add `agent:<A>` only when A is claude/codex/cursor (if edit fails because a label is missing, retry without the remove/agent label and warn). Print: title + url, the issue body, IN FLIGHT (other in-progress issues: # title assignees) and OVERLAPS between this issue's Scope paths and files in open PRs (prefix or fnmatch match), then a short NEXT STEPS reminder: context via `entire search`/`entire graph query`/`entire brain brief`, small commits staging files by name, `./hq check`, `./hq pr N --body-file .context/pr-N.md`.
5. `release N [--needs-human] [--note TEXT] [--agent A] [--workspace W]`: post release marker (+ note). Labels: remove status:in-progress, add status:needs-human if flag else status:ready. Remove assignee @me only if no other active claim by my login remains.
6. `pr N --body-file F [--draft] [--agent A] [--allow-dirty] [--no-rebase-check]`: refuse on default branch; refuse if `git status --porcelain` is non-empty (unless --allow-dirty); `git fetch origin <default>` and, if `origin/<default>` exists and is not an ancestor of HEAD (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`), refuse with `rebase first: git rebase origin/<default>, then ./hq check` (unless --no-rebase-check); `git push -u origin HEAD`. Title `<issue title> (#N)`; body = file contents + `\n\nCloses #N\n\n---\nAgent: `<id>``. If an open PR for this head branch exists (`gh pr list --head <branch> --state open --json number,url`), `gh pr edit` title/body; else `gh pr create --base <default> --head <branch> --title ... --body-file -` (+ --draft). Copy issue labels matching `lane:*`, `P0/P1/P2`, `agent:*`, `size:*`, `type:*` onto the PR. Issue: add status:review, remove status:in-progress. Print the PR URL and NEXT STEPS: `entire trail create --title "<title> (#N)" --type feature`, `entire trail ci-pr`, `entire review` unless size:S, then `gh pr edit <PR> --add-label review:pass` and `entire trail ready`.
7. `ship PR [--skip-review]`: `gh pr view PR --json number,title,state,isDraft,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,labels,statusCheckRollup,headRefName,closingIssuesReferences,url`; if mergeable is UNKNOWN retry up to 3x with a 2s sleep. Gates (print each failing gate, exit 2): state OPEN, not draft, not CONFLICTING, checks: every CheckRun has status COMPLETED with conclusion SUCCESS/NEUTRAL/SKIPPED and every StatusContext has state SUCCESS (pending -> refuse "checks still running"; zero checks is OK), label review:pass present unless --skip-review. Merge with `gh pr merge PR --squash` (NO --delete-branch: it breaks inside worktrees; the repo setting deletes the remote branch). Then unblock: for open issues labelled status:blocked, parse `Blocked by`; if all refs are now closed, add status:ready, remove status:blocked, comment `Unblocked: #X merged in #PR`. Print merged PR and the unblocked issues.
8. `check`: run each `hq.json` `check` command (shell=True, capture output); print `✓ <cmd> (1.2s)` or `✗ <cmd> (exit N)` followed by the last 30 lines of its output; run all; exit 1 if any failed. If none configured print `no checks configured yet (hq.json "check")` and exit 0.

Unit-test at least: section parsing incl. `_No response_` and `none`, issue-ref parsing, scope-path parsing, active-claim computation (release later/earlier, two ids, ties), winner selection, slugify, overlap map, scope-vs-file matching, stale detection, check-rollup evaluation (success/pending/failure/StatusContext/empty), ship gate evaluation, ready-queue sorting.

When done, also run `./hq --help`, `./hq check`, and `./hq setup --check` (read-only) and include their output (trimmed) in your report. Report: files created, test count/result, any deviation from this spec and why. Keep the report under 300 words.

I'm confirming that the system Python here is 3.9.6, so I can use it to check 3.9 compatibility. Next I'll write the tests before the implementation, starting with the pure functions, beginning with `parse_sections`, which splits the issue body into `### Heading` sections.

I'm settling on how `parse_sections` keys its output: lowercased headings, so lookups don't depend on case. For `parse_issue_refs`, I'll accept `#N` references and `/issues/N` or `/pull/N` URLs, returning unique numbers in order and treating `none` as an empty list. I'm still weighing whether bare numbers like "12, 14" should count too, since that could pick up stray digits.

I'm weighing whether to also accept bare numbers like "12, 14" when there's no `#` reference, since that would make "Blocked by: 12" work too. The risk is that a stray digit gets read as an issue number, so I'm leaning toward accepting only whole numeric tokens and testing that case.

I'm defining `active_claims` to walk the comments in chronological order, recording each claim marker and dropping any claim for an id that a later release marker for that same id has cleared. What's left are the claims still in effect.

I'm sorting the claim and release markers by timestamp, with list order as the tiebreaker, so a release at the same moment as a claim still counts as later. I'll parse the ISO 8601 timestamps into datetimes instead of comparing strings, since Python 3.9 doesn't accept the trailing "Z" directly and that has to be handled.

I'm checking how `fromisoformat` treats the trailing "Z" and fractional seconds on 3.9, since that decides how timestamps get parsed. Next I'm sorting out the per-id rule: each id should keep only its earliest active claim, so a claim that was released and then made again counts as the newest one.

I'm working out how a claim should behave when the same id already holds it. Re-claiming should be idempotent, so I won't post a duplicate claim comment. If another id holds an earlier active claim, the command should refuse with exit 2.

I'm weighing the order of operations for the claim: checking the issue state, blocking refs, and the current winner first, then handling the branch. Since the claim comment records the branch name, I'm considering whether to compute the name and post the claim before actually switching branches, so a lost race doesn't leave a stray branch behind.

I'm settling the claim order: if the branch is the default or detached, I switch to a new branch first and only then post the claim, re-fetch comments, and release if I didn't win. Since a branch may already exist after a release, I'll check for it and switch to it rather than creating it again.

I'm working out the claim flow for Conductor workspaces, where each one is a worktree on its own branch, so the current branch usually isn't the default and the claim can use it directly. After posting the claim comment, I re-fetch the comments and compare the winner; if someone else won, I post a release noting the lost race and exit with code 3. Then I'm planning the `gh issue edit` call to add the assignee and in-progress label and remove the ready label, falling back to a version without the label changes and a warning if a label doesn't exist yet.

I'm working out how to handle the case where removing a label fails: gh may reject `--remove-label` for a label that doesn't exist in the repo.
